title: WAL hash probing and frame page-number lookup

scope.rationale: walHash, walNextHash, and walFramePgno form the allocation-free WAL-index addressing core: they compute the initial power-of-two slot, advance collision probes with wraparound, and resolve a frame to its database page number across the smaller first index page and later full pages.

external_source_responsibilities: Mapped WAL-index page arrays and source frame-page partition constants
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete active bodies are assigned. WAL index append/find, undo, recovery, and checkpoint owners call the hash and frame-page-number helpers through the typed native Wal owner.

inputs: Nonzero database page number, prior hash slot, or positive WAL frame number with a mapped index page
outputs: Initial hash slot, wrapped next slot, or database page number recorded for the frame
contracts.ownership: Borrowed scalar or WAL-index page slices; no allocation, release, or mutation.
contracts.state_and_results: Hash multiplication wraps at u32 width before the slot mask. Probe advancement wraps at the power-of-two slot count. Frame lookup applies the smaller first-page offset and full later-page modulo exactly.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Caller owns WAL-index locks and valid mappings. No callbacks or direct I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Zero/out-of-range frames are rejected by the typed boundary; valid inputs leave WAL state unchanged.

representation_differences: The C WAL-index header offset is represented by IndexPage.page_numbers already sliced past metadata on the first typed index page.
The typed helper returns Range for frame zero or an unavailable array position instead of relying on source caller assertions and mapped-memory invariants.

oracle.protocol: Exercise initial and maximum-u32 page hashes, probe wraparound, first/last first-page frames, and the first frame on the second WAL-index page, then retain the maintained WAL differential for integrated append/find/checkpoint callers.
oracle.normalization: Scalar slots, offsets, page numbers, and errors are exact; mapped addresses are not observed.

assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No direct I/O; callers own mapped-index locking and publication.
assurance.malformed_input: Typed zero/out-of-range frame guards supplement source assertions without weakening valid-frame behavior.
assurance.continuation: Pure lookups do not mutate WAL state.
assurance.performance: Constant-time arithmetic and one indexed page-number load.

integration.native_call_path: indexAppend uses hashPage/nextHash; undo, recovery, checkpoint, and frame search use framePageNumber.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: No duplicate typed hash or frame-page-number owner remains.

independent_review.notes: Requires exact pinned-C scalar trace, mapped-index concurrency assurance, and independent review.

known_blockers: Add an exact pinned-C scalar trace before internal-trace promotion.
Mapped WAL-index publication and concurrent-reader assurance remain broader subsystem work.

implementation_spans: upstream/sqlite/src/wal.c:1132-1225 was reviewed completely for hash constants, collision wraparound, hash-page partitioning, first-page metadata offset, and later-page modulo lookup
src/core/internal/wal_core.zig hashPage, nextHash, framePage, hashGet, framePageNumber, and their production callers were reviewed
callers: walIndexAppend inserts page numbers using walHash/walNextHash
WAL undo, recovery, checkpoint iteration, and frame lookup consume walFramePgno-equivalent results
callees: Hash arithmetic uses only fixed constants
Frame lookup consumes typed hashGet/framePage and one mapped page_numbers entry
assertions_branches_cleanup: All seven active behavior blocks are assigned
Hash power-of-two and nonzero-page assumptions are retained
First and later index-page branches are represented by framePage plus zero-relative page slices
upstream_tests: Upstream WAL, walro, wal2, checkpoint, savepoint, corruption, and recovery tests cover these helpers through callers
Project WAL unit and differential tests cover hash insertion plus first/second index-page lookup
